step-1.text: Build it in the room it will live in. Spread the parts out on the empty boxes and check the hardware bags against the parts list first.

count-1.text: Nothing new this step. Just you and the frame.

step-2.text: Stand the head end frame up and bolt the two lower side rails to it, one at the back and one at the front. Slat ledges face in. Hand tight for now.

count-2.text: This step uses 1 end frame, 2 side rails and 4 bolts.

step-3.text: Bring in the foot end frame and bolt the free ends of the rails to it. A helper holds the frame upright while you start each bolt.

count-3.text: This step uses 1 end frame and 4 bolts.

step-4.text: Now the top bunk. Lift each upper side rail into place between the end frames and bolt both ends. Use a step stool, not the bed, to reach.

count-4.text: This step uses 2 side rails and 8 bolts.

step-5.text: Measure corner to corner across the frame both ways. When the diagonals match it is square. Now tighten every bolt, firmly.

count-5.text: Nothing new this step. Just you and the frame.

step-6.text: Drop the metal support bars in down the middle, end frame to end frame, and screw each one in. They keep the slats from sagging.

count-6.text: This step uses 2 metal support bars and 4 screws.

step-7.text: Unroll the lower slat roll across the ledges and screw or clip the ends down. Fifteen slats, evenly spaced.

step-8.text: Same up top: unroll the slats across the upper ledges and fix both ends. Fifteen slats. Check none of them can slide out.

step-9.text: Bolt the long guard rail along the back of the top bunk, and the short one along the front, leaving the gap for the ladder. Both sides of the top get a rail, even against a wall.

count-9.text: This step uses 2 guard rails and 8 bolts.

step-10.text: Hook the ladder over the front rail in the gap and bolt it on at the top. Its feet sit flat on the floor.

count-10.text: This step uses 1 ladder and 2 bolts.

step-11.text: Push the bed against a wall and give it a firm shake: nothing should rock or creak. A tall bed is top-heavy, so anchor it to the wall with fixings for your wall. The top bunk is not for children under six.

done.text: Done. Your CLASSIC twin over twin bunk bed is built. Give it a proud little pat.
